thread:
support_sam: Heads-up — ACME reported a big latency regression on /v1/generate around 09:12 UTC. p95 jumped from ~300ms to ~2.8s and p99 is ~10s for the last 15m. They're also seeing ~3% 503/504s. Customer says this started after a burst of traffic from one of their tenants.

support_sam: Repro steps provided by customer: quick loop of 50 concurrent requests, each ~1k tokens. They can reproduce consistently.

carmen_eng: Thanks, looking. Can you paste the request IDs or sample traces? Also which model/route?

support_sam: Sample request_id: req_20260315_acme_01, route: /v1/generate (model: rdx-7b-q4) — they said they were doing parallel inference from a single client IP.

oncall-bot: New alert — high_queue_length on service-infer-7b (threshold 50). Current queue length: 128.

oncall-bot: Autoscale event suppressed due to reserved-capacity floor.

raj_oncall: I'm on it. First guess: worker pool saturated / admission control hitting concurrency cap, causing long queueing delays. Carmen, can you check worker GPU utilization and queueing metrics? Lina can check admission controller logs.

carmen_eng: Looking at infra metrics now. GPU utilization on the 7b pool is 95-99% across nodes; running tasks per GPU is at max concurrency. KV cache hit rate dropped to 4% from ~60% (might be cache thrash due to varied prefixes). Batch sizes are high (avg 12), but latency jump suggests requests are waiting in the admission queue.

lina_infra: Admission controller logs show repeated "admit-deny: concurrency_exceeded" for tenant acme-123 between 09:12:08 — 09:25:00. Their tenant has a per-tenant concurrency cap of 40; we see bursts trying to exceed that. Also repeated requeue attempts causing pileup.

support_sam: Customer says they expect occasional bursts and asked why autoscale didn't kick earlier.

carmen_eng: Autoscale is using reserved-capacity policy for this Dedicated pool; we have a hard floor and 10m cooldown. Plus burst capacity is exhausted (they used burst earlier this morning).

raj_oncall: Mitigations to try (short-term):
1) Temporarily raise tenant concurrency for acme-123 from 40 -> 80 for 15 minutes.
2) Enable immediate fallback to rdx-3b for overflowed requests for this tenant (reduce latency and compute).
3) Throttle long requests (>2k tokens) to use queued-priority low to avoid blocking short requests.

carmen_eng: I'll push a transient config change to increase concurrency for acme-123 and enable model-fallback. Running command:

```
# grant temporary concurrency override
redwoodctl tenants update acme-123 --concurrency-override 80 --ttl 15m
# enable fallback policy for tenant
redwoodctl routes update /v1/generate --tenant acme-123 --fallback-model rdx-3b
```

lina_infra: Also patching admission controller to reject immediately (fast-fail) for connections that would exceed queue depth >200 so we avoid unbounded pileup. Pushing rule now.

oncall-bot: Config change applied: acme-123 concurrency override -> 80 (expires in 15m). Fallback rdx-3b enabled on /v1/generate for acme-123. Admission rule fast-fail set at queue_depth=200.

support_sam: Customer confirmed improved p95 after change: dropped to ~420ms within 90s. They're still seeing occasional p99 spikes ~2s when they hit sustained 300 concurrent short requests.

carmen_eng: That's expected — fallback reduces compute and queue but doesn't restore KV cache locality. Suggest we enable prefix caching for their hot prompts (we can add an LRU for their tenant). Liaising with customer to identify hot prefixes.

support_sam: Customer provided a set of 12 prompt prefixes — they agreed to try prefix-level caching.

raj_oncall: Medium-term actions:
- Add tenant-specific burst policy linked to billing tier (so reserved floor isn't abused but burst is allowed with short metering).
- Improve autoscale to consider queue length + avg latency, not just CPU/GPU utilization.
- Add admission-controller telemetry to surface per-tenant deny rates in console.

lina_infra: Filing infra ticket INFRA-2026 to add queue-length trigger to autoscaler and expose per-tenant deny metrics.

carmen_eng: For root-cause notes: overloaded workers + cold KV cache + hard tenant concurrency cap + exhausted burst capacity = queue waterfall. Burst from single tenant amplified due to cache misses.

support_sam: Customer asked about billing/credits for throttled requests. I explained failed/fast-fail requests are not billed; queued requests that succeed are billed as usual. They want SLA language updated.

raj_oncall: Closing loop: keep concurrency override for 15m and monitor. If p95 remains >1s after fallback + caching, plan emergency drain/reshuffle (move some jobs to standby pool).

carmen_eng: Monitoring: p95 for /v1/generate now 380-500ms, p99 under 1.8s. Queue length down to 16. I will follow up with a postmortem summary and recommended platform changes.

support_sam: Thanks team. I'll update the customer and ask them to run controlled burst tests after we enable prefix caching.

customer_acme_bot: acme-ops: Confirming we see improvement. Will coordinate controlled replay at 14:00 UTC. Thanks. :thumbsup:

lina_infra: Next steps (internal): INFRA-2026 (autoscale queue trigger), INFRA-2027 (per-tenant deny metrics), PLATFORM-3982 (tenant burst policy + billing adjustments). Assigning to infra/product.

raj_oncall: Marking this thread as resolved for support. Reopen if regressions after caching / replay.

support_sam: closing thread — will attach postmortem link when available. :white_check_mark:
